metas.name: -Ach ending
metas.note: In the southern half of Germany many Towns/villages use the -ach ending
metas.footer: I made this map with all locations for the suffixes.

metas.name: -Itz ending
metas.note: In the eastern part of Germany many Towns/villages use the -itz ending
metas.footer: I made this map with all locations for the suffixes.

metas.name: -Ow ending
metas.note: In the north-eastern part of Germany many Towns/villages use the -ow ending
metas.footer: I made this map with all locations for the suffixes.

metas.name: A-Type Guardrail
metas.note:
While most of Germany uses B-Type guardrails, some regions predominantly use A-Type instead. Learning which regions use them can be useful.

NOTE: There will always be rare exceptions. For a good overview of European guardrails, see this infographic.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Aldi
metas.note: There are two regional Aldi chains, which have split Germany in two; Aldi Süd in the south, and Aldi Nord in the north.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Area Code 2
metas.note: Covers most of North Rhine-Westphalia, northern Rhineland-Palatinate, and parts of Hesse. NOTE: Area codes starting with 01 are mobile and therefore not region-specific.
metas.footer: Plonk It Germany & Jerome´s doc and own discoveries

metas.name: Area Code 3
metas.note: Includes Berlin, Brandenburg, Saxony, Thuringia, and parts of Saxony-Anhalt. NOTE: Area codes starting with 01 are mobile and therefore not region-specific.
metas.footer: Plonk It Germany & Jerome´s doc and own discoveries

metas.name: Area Code 4
metas.note: Covers Hamburg, Bremen, Schleswig-Holstein, and coastal Lower Saxony. NOTE: Area codes starting with 01 are mobile and therefore not region-specific.
metas.footer: Plonk It Germany & Jerome´s doc and own discoveries

metas.name: Area Code 5
metas.note: Includes Lower Saxony, northern Hesse, and parts of North Rhine-Westphalia. NOTE: Area codes starting with 01 are mobile and therefore not region-specific.
metas.footer: Plonk It Germany & Jerome´s doc and own discoveries

metas.name: Area Code 6
metas.note: Covers Saarland, Rhineland-Palatinate, central and southern Hesse, and parts of Bavaria and Baden-Württemberg. NOTE: Area codes starting with 01 are mobile and therefore not region-specific.
metas.footer: Plonk It Germany & Jerome´s doc and own discoveries

metas.name: Area Code 7
metas.note: Includes most of Baden-Württemberg and parts of Rhineland-Palatinate and Bavaria. NOTE: Area codes starting with 01 are mobile and therefore not region-specific.
metas.footer: Plonk It Germany & Jerome´s doc and own discoveries

metas.name: Area Code 8
metas.note: Covers southern Bavaria. NOTE: Area codes starting with 01 are mobile and therefore not region-specific.
metas.footer: Plonk It Germany & Jerome´s doc and own discoveries

metas.name: Area Code 9
metas.note: Includes northern Bavaria, parts of Thuringia, Hesse, and Baden-Württemberg. NOTE: Area codes starting with 01 are mobile and therefore not region-specific.
metas.footer: Plonk It Germany & Jerome´s doc and own discoveries

metas.name: B Type Guardrail
metas.note: In Germany there are both B-/ and A-Type Guardrail. Learning which regions can be useful.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Baden-Württemberg
metas.note: Baden-Württemberg uses this grey desgin with white plates on its triangular posts. NOTE: The grey colour can be washed out and the post can look white
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Baden-Württemberg
metas.note: Similarly, Baden-Württemberg is the only state where the plates on the bollards can be grey instead of white. They also can freature two black stripes at the top and bottom.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Bavaria Road Marker
metas.note: Bavaria uses these white rectangular road markers, which are divided by black lines into three sections. The left section provides the road you are currently on.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Bavaria Wooden Bollards
metas.note: These round wooden bollards, which have a painted top, are found in Bavaria.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Bavarian Church
metas.note: Bavarian churches often have a rounded top on the tower. NOTE: This can be found in BW rarely.
metas.footer: Plonk It Germany & Jerome´s doc and own discoveries

metas.name: Berlin Bus Stop
metas.note: Berlin uses segmented bus stops, with a yellow signpost. Its often seen together with the trash bin.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Berlin Street Signs
metas.note: Berlin uses white signs with a grey border, and a separate section for numbers under the street name. Also note how the letter ß looks.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Berlin Trash Bin
metas.note: Berlin uses bright orange bins that have white text on them. Its often seen together with the bus stop.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Bielefeld Yellow Bands
metas.note: Bielefeld has these yellow bands around they´re stop lights all over the city.
metas.footer: Plonk It Germany & Jerome´s doc and own discoveries

metas.name: Black Forest Architecture
metas.note: In rural central-southern parts of the Black Forest you can find this pretty unique architecture with often low roofs and long balconies.
metas.footer: @jerome8746´s doc

metas.name: Bollard Top
metas.note: Some bollards in North Rhine-Westphalia have a green bit at the top. The top can also be another colour.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Brandenburg Post
metas.note: Fully yellow posts are found in the state of Brandenburg.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Bremen Bus Stop
metas.note: Bremen proper uses simple bus stops, which have the bus stop name within a red section. The edges can be rounded. Its often seen together with the trash bin.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Bremen Trashbin
metas.note: Bremen has green and grey bins, with orange speech bubbles. Its often seen together with the bus stop sign.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Bremerhavem Trash Bin
metas.note: Bremerhaven trash bins use a more generic green design, with a black logo. Its often seen together with the bus stop sign.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Bremerhaven Bus Stop
metas.note: Bremerhaven, which is still part of Bremen, uses bus stops with a grey section on the opposite side of the signpost. And the bus stop name is red within a yellow section. Its often seen together with the trash bin.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Cologne Lamppost Markings
metas.note:
Lampposts in Cologne will often feature these bright yellow numbers on a black piece of plastic.

NOTE: Similar looking things can be found elsewhere as well.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Commie Blocks
metas.note: These large, utilitarian apartment buildings constructed during the socialist era, that are also known as “Commie blocks” are common in all of former East Germany.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Dortmund Street Sign
metas.note: Dortmund uses different blue variants in a grey frame, but the sign has a seperate section for numbers.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Dresden Street Signs
metas.note: Dresden has blue street signs with a unique font.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Drink Market Fristo
metas.note: Fristo is a drink market chain. Its common in the south half and the east of Germany, its easy recognizable with its unique sign being often visible from roads.
metas.footer: Doc

metas.name: East Pole
metas.note: This round concrete pole with metal straps around it is most common in Saxony but also generally in eastern Germany.
metas.footer: Plonk It Germany & Jerome´s doc and own discoveries

metas.name: Eastern Pole
metas.note: Concrete Pole with split bar on top. The middle part is thicker and the insulators are a little bit longer and thicker. NOTE: this can be confused with other Poles existing everywhere!
metas.footer: doc

metas.name: German Alps
metas.note: The German Alps is the most mountainous region in Germany, it is mostly concentrated on the Austrian Border.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Green Tree Marks
metas.note: Many trees in Brandenburg and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern have these tiny green markers on them. You can very rarely find them in Lower Saxony.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Half-timbered with Arches
metas.note: This type of half-timbered house with arches at the ground floor is very common in this region of Saxony.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Hamburg Bus Stop
metas.note: Hamburg bus stops have a red signpost, and the route numbers are within hexagons. Note that they can be found outside of Hamburg as well. They are often seen together with the trash bin.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Hamburg Trash Bin
metas.note: Hamburg uses bright red bins, with white speech bubbles. Also they are most often seen with the bus stop.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Hop
metas.note: Hop is are most common seen above Munich. Also there is a dense area above "Friedrichshafen" above the Lake of Constance.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Loop Guardrail Ending
metas.note: A Loop ending of the guardrail is common in Brandenburg, Berlin and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania (especially in brandenburg)
metas.footer: Plonk It Germany & Jerome´s doc and own discoveries

metas.name: Lowcam
metas.note: **Lowcam **coverage can be found around Singen and near Switzerland.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: LVR Bollard Top
metas.note: Some of the green caps will have the text ‘LVR’, along with a small coat of arms. These specific green caps are unique to southern North Rhine-Westphalia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Magdeburg Trams/Busses
metas.note: Magdeburg uses green-(orange)-white trams and busses. They have "MVB" (Magdeburger Verkehrs Betriebe) in a special font on them. Trams can freature large ads. NOTE: They can be red but will always have the "MVB" on them.
metas.footer: Doc

metas.name: Mainz Street Sign
metas.note: Mainz has a mix of blue signs, and this unique red variant.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Munich Bus Stops
metas.note: Munich uses specific Bus Stops. They commonly have this blue design with the rounded top, on boards to each side it displays the stops name which can be used to regionguess.
metas.footer: Doc

metas.name: Munich Street Signs
metas.note: Munich has blue street signs with a white decorative border that does not touch the corners. Also note the unique font. NOTE: While the blue design itsself is common elsewhere the font is unique
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Munich surroundings Bus Stop
metas.note: The area around Munich (13 Lkr.) use a unique blue bus stop design with a green frame and MVV written on its bottom. NOTE: not common in the city of Munich
metas.footer: Doc

metas.name: Munich Trams/busses
metas.note:
Munich uses specific trams/busses they most commoly have a

  • blue design and have the name of the public transport company
  • "MVG" printed on them.
  • In they front they often show the Munich coat of arms.
  • The trams can have large ads on them.
metas.footer: Doc

metas.name: Northwestern Architecture
metas.note:
These brick houses are generally concentrated in northwestern Germany.

NOTE: This map is very approximate.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: NRW Sign Posts
metas.note: North Rhine-Westphalia can use these unique sign posts for pedestrian crossings. NOTE: They are rare but unique
metas.footer: @jerome8746´s doc

metas.name: NRW Triangular Post
metas.note: North Rhine-Westphalia uses white posts without white plates on the sides. You can also find posts which go all the way to the ground.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Odd Bollard
metas.note: These irregular looking bollards, which do not have a white encasing on the bottom half, are found on K-roads in this region of Lower Saxony. K-Roads in this region will not have any other type of bollard.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Pineforests
metas.note:
Baltic Pines or Pinus sylvestris are generally more concentrated in the northeast of Germany. They can be recognized by their orange-tinged trunk.

NOTE: This map is very approximate.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Postal Code 0xxxx
metas.note: Includes parts of Saxony, southern Saxony-Anhalt, southern Brandenburg, and eastern Thuringia. The postal code can be found in adresses
metas.footer: Plonk It Germany & Jerome´s doc and own discoveries

metas.name: Postal Code 1xxxx
metas.note: Covers Berlin, most of Brandenburg and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, plus small parts of Lower Saxony and Saxony-Anhalt.
metas.footer: Plonk It Germany & Jerome´s doc and own discoveries

metas.name: Postal Code 2xxxx
metas.note: Covers Hamburg, Schleswig-Holstein, northern Lower Saxony, Bremen, and a small part of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania.
metas.footer: Plonk It Germany & Jerome´s doc and own discoveries

metas.name: Postal Code 3xxxx
metas.note: Includes southern Lower Saxony, eastern North Rhine-Westphalia, northern Hesse, Thuringia, and parts of Saxony-Anhalt.
metas.footer: Plonk It Germany & Jerome´s doc and own discoveries

metas.name: Postal Code 4xxxx
metas.note: Used in northwestern North Rhine-Westphalia and southwestern Lower Saxony.
metas.footer: Plonk It Germany & Jerome´s doc and own discoveries

metas.name: Postal Code 5xxxx
metas.note: Covers southwestern North Rhine-Westphalia, large parts of Rhineland-Palatinate, and parts of Hesse.
metas.footer: Plonk It Germany & Jerome´s doc and own discoveries

metas.name: Postal Code 6xxxx
metas.note: Includes southern Hesse, Rhineland-Palatinate, Saarland, and small parts of Bavaria and Baden-Württemberg.
metas.footer: Plonk It Germany & Jerome´s doc and own discoveries

metas.name: Postal Code 7xxxx
metas.note: Covers most of Baden-Württemberg and small areas of Rhineland-Palatinate.
metas.footer: Plonk It Germany & Jerome´s doc and own discoveries

metas.name: Postal Code 8xxxx
metas.note: Found in southern Bavaria and the southeastern part of Baden-Württemberg.
metas.footer: Plonk It Germany & Jerome´s doc and own discoveries

metas.name: Postal Code 9xxxx
metas.note: Covers northern Bavaria, large parts of Thuringia, and a small part of Baden-Württemberg.
metas.footer: Plonk It Germany & Jerome´s doc and own discoveries

metas.name: Red Cap Posts
metas.note: These white posts with a red cap are found in all of former East Germany, but most commonly in the state of Saxony-Anhalt.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Red Cycling Sign
metas.note: North Rhine-Westphalia & Hamburg are using a red cycling sign desing.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Regensburg Plains
metas.note: The flat plains southeast of Regensburg can be recognised by the slight ridge often visible to the northeast. The plains themselves are flat, and quite agricultural.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Rhineland-Palatinate Orange Bollards
metas.note: Rhineland-Palatinate is the only state where the plates on the bollards are orange instead of white.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Saarland Cycling Signs
metas.note: Saarland uses a green cycling sign.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Saxony-Anhalt Red Bollard
metas.note: This red bollard can rarely be found in Saxony-Anhalt.
metas.footer: Plonk It Germany & Jerome´s doc and own discoveries

metas.name: Saxony-Anhalt Yellow Posts
metas.note:
Yellow posts with a white plate on them are found in Saxony-Anhalt.

NOTE: Sometimes there is only 1 plate, which can make it hard to tell apart from a Brandenburg post.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Schleswig-Holstein Architecture
metas.note: Thatched roofs and rock walls are most common on the North Frisian Islands, as well as mainland Schleswig-Holstein. You can also commonly find them in coastal resort towns in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Sign Back Connectors
metas.note:
You can use the sign back connectors on street signs to regionguess Germany.

NOTE: The double connector on triangular signs are generally wider. T-shaped connectors may look like this.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Sign Back Folded/not Folded
metas.note:
You can use the sign backs of street signs to regionguess Germany.

Here are examples of a folded, and flat sign back.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Simple Orange Posts
metas.note: These simple orange posts are most commonly found in Bavaria, and also in the other highlighted states.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Slate Walls
metas.note: Houses with black slate walls, resembling fish scales, are commonly found in a large area of central Germany.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Sorbian
metas.note: Sorbian, a Slavic language, is spoken near the Polish and Czech border. You can find it on a variety of signs in these regions.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: South Germany Architecture
metas.note: In the south of the country you can find big houses with traditional wooden details, often featuring balconies with flowers.
metas.footer: Plonk It Germany & Jerome´s doc and own discoveries

metas.name: Stuttgart Tram Rails
metas.note: In the entire city of Stuttgart, there are a lot of roads with these kind off tram rails in the middle.
metas.footer: doc

metas.name: Suffix "-beck"
metas.note: The suffix "-beck" can be found in the northern half of the country
metas.footer: suffix map (1/3)

metas.name: Suffix "-büll"
metas.note: In the north(west) of Schleswig-Holstein right next to the Danish border, 30 places use the suffix "-büll" in their name.
metas.footer: suffix map (2/3)

metas.name: Suffix "-by"
metas.note: In the north(east) of Schleswig-Holstein, 49 places use the suffix "-by" in their names.
metas.footer: suffix map (2/3)

metas.name: Suffix "-hofen"
metas.note: The suffix "-hofen" can be found in the southern half of the country.
metas.footer: suffix map (1/3)

metas.name: Suffix "-rath"
metas.note: In the west of NRW, parts of Rhineland-Palatinate and Saarland, 144 places use the suffix "-rath" in their name.
metas.footer: suffix map (2/3)

metas.name: Suffix "-ried"
metas.note: The suffix "-ried" can be found in some parts of the southern half of the country.
metas.footer: suffix map (1/3)

metas.name: Suffix "-roth"
metas.note: There are 124 places using the suffix "-roth"
metas.footer: suffix map (3/3)

metas.name: Suffix "-scheid"
metas.note: In NRW, parts of Rhineland-Palatinate and Saarland, 195 places use the suffix "-scheid" in their name. NOTE: there 3 of them elsewhere.
metas.footer: suffix map (2/3)

metas.name: Suffix "-stetten"
metas.note: The suffix "-stetten" is can be found in the southern half of the country
metas.footer: suffix map (1/3)

metas.name: Suffix "hoven"
metas.note: In the area southwest of Düsseldorf and around Bonn you can find 36 places using the suffix "hoven"
metas.footer: suffix map (2/3)

metas.name: Sylt
metas.note:
The shrub and sand covered hills are unique to the island of Sylt. And like the rest of the North Frisian Islands, rock walls, brick houses, and thatched roofs are common.

NOTE: Some parts of Sylt look more generic, but still very flat.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Vineyards
metas.note: Vineyards are mostly concentrated in the southwest of Germany. However, there are a couple regions as well. So if there are wineyards you are most likely not far away from Rhine River.
metas.footer: Plonk It Germany & Jerome´s doc and own discoveries

metas.name: Weiler
metas.note: In the southwest of Germany many Towns/villages use "Weiler" in their names. For small villages these signs are sometimes yellow on green and for bigger black on yellow.
metas.footer: I made this map with all locations for the suffixes.

metas.name: West Mannheim Architecture
metas.note: Orange/brownish brick can be found west of Mannheim (to the french border)
metas.footer: Plonk It Germany & Jerome´s doc and own discoveries

metas.name: White Black Gen 4 Car
metas.note:
You can find this rare white and black Generation 4 car in Hamburg and around Frankfurt.

NOTE: You can also find the same car around London and in Ireland.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: White Tree Markings
metas.note:
You can spot trees that are painted white close to the bottom of the trunk in the northeast.

NOTE: You will rarely find them outside the shaded region.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Wooden Shingle Facade
metas.note: These wooden shingles are called "Schindeln" they are common on older farmshouses or other traditional build houses in southgermany.
metas.footer: Doc
